summary: A travel guide from The Independent listing the best UK locations to see the Northern Lights (aurora borealis), as sightings have become more frequent and reached as far south as Wiltshire in February 2023. It covers destinations in Scotland, England and Wales, with notes on seasons, dark sky status and viewing spots. Sightings can't be predicted, and light-pollution-free northern and coastal areas are generally best.
one_line: A guide to eight UK regions in Scotland, England and Wales offering the best chances of seeing the Northern Lights, with seasons and viewing tips.
key_facts: The Northern Lights occur when electronically charged particles enter Earth's atmosphere from space, producing green, yellow, purple and even red displays.
The aurora was seen as far south as Wiltshire in February 2023.
The Outer Hebrides, likely Lewis or Harris, are the best bet in the Hebrides; the season runs September to April and the Isle of Lewis hosts a Dark Skies Festival in February.
Shetland is the most northerly point in Britain, over 100 miles from the mainland, with a season from mid-October to mid-March and less than six hours of daylight on the shortest days.
The Cairngorms are the UK's largest National Park and include the Tomintoul and Glenlivet International Dark Sky Park around the Glenlivet Estate.
The Yorkshire Dales saw the aurora as recently as April 2023, have four Dark Sky Discovery sites, and will host a joint Dark Skies Festival with the North York Moors National Park in February 2024.
The Yorkshire Dales park says up to 2,000 stars can be seen on clear nights; the Perseid meteor shower occurs in August.

Northumberland's National Park is an International Dark Sky Park reportedly with the darkest skies in the UK; lights are usually visible only after strong geomagnetic storms, with past sightings over Hadrian's Wall and Bamburgh.
Snowdonia is one of three Dark Sky reserves in Wales, covers 823 square miles, and has 1,497 miles of public footpaths.
Best Snowdonia viewing spots are Llyn Geirionydd, Llyn y Dywarchen and Ty Cipar, between Llan Ffestiniog and Ysbyty Ifan.
The Lake District is seeking International Dark Sky Reserve status, with good viewpoints at Grizedale Forest, Wasdale, the Langdale Valley and Derwentwater.
Coastal areas are often better for aurora viewing because there are fewer clouds.
